sources.title: Association Between Biomarkers of Ovarian Reserve and Infertility Among Older Women of Reproductive Age
sources.claim: 750 women aged 30-44 trying for 3 months or less; low AMH (<0.7 ng/mL) vs normal: conceived by 6 cycles 65% vs 62%, by 12 cycles 84% vs 75%; low reserve biomarkers not associated with reduced fertility.
sources.quote: probability of conceiving by 6 cycles ... 65% vs 62% ... by 12 cycles 84% vs 75% ... lower ovarian reserve biomarkers were not associated with reduced fertility

sources.title: Optimizing natural fertility: a committee opinion
sources.claim: Fertile window is the 6 days ending on ovulation; intercourse every 1-2 days in the window is most efficient; about 80% conceive in first 6 months; fecundability highest in first 3 months; relative fertility about half at 40; men little affected before about 50; caffeine 500 mg+ linked to lower fertility, 1-2 cups no clear harm; avoid >2 drinks/day; smoking OR 1.60; folic acid at least 400 mcg; apps max 21% accuracy for ovulation day; peak mucus day ~38%.
sources.quote: the 6-day interval ending on the day of ovulation ... every 1 to 2 days during the fertile window ... Approximately 80% of couples will conceive in the first 6 months ... decreased by about half at age 40 ... maximum accuracy of 21% in predicting the day of ovulation

sources.title: Definition of infertility: a committee opinion
sources.claim: Evaluation should start at 12 months when the female partner is under 35 and at 6 months at 35 or older; nothing in the definition should delay treatment for anyone regardless of relationship status or orientation.
sources.quote: evaluation should be initiated at 12 months when the female partner is under 35 years of age ... at 6 months when the female partner is 35 years of age or older

sources.title: Timing of sexual intercourse in relation to ovulation
sources.claim: 221 healthy women; conception only with intercourse in the 6 days ending on ovulation day; probability 33% when intercourse was on the day of ovulation.
sources.quote: We recruited 221 healthy women ... Conception occurred only when intercourse took place during a six-day period that ended on the estimated day of ovulation ... 0.33 when it occurred on the day of ovulation itself

sources.title: Fertility problems: assessment and treatment (NG257), initial advice
sources.claim: Over 80% of couples with woman under 40 conceive within 1 year, cumulative over 90% at 2 years; by age at 1 year/2 years: 19-26 92%/98%, 27-29 87%/95%, 30-34 86%/94%, 35-39 82%/90%; sex every 2 to 3 days; table assumes twice a week.
sources.quote: over 80% of heterosexual couples in the general population will conceive within 1 year ... 19-26 years: 92% ... 98% ... 35-39 years: 82% ... 90% ... every 2 to 3 days optimises the chance of pregnancy

sources.title: About Folic Acid
sources.claim: 400 mcg folic acid daily, starting at least 1 month before conception.
sources.quote: the U.S. Public Health Service recommends that you get 400 mcg of folic acid daily ... start taking folic acid at least 1 month before conception

sources.title: Diagnosis and treatment of infertility in men: AUA/ASRM guideline part I
sources.claim: Initial male evaluation should include a reproductive history and one or more semen analyses; at least two, ideally a month apart, especially if the first is abnormal.
sources.quote: Initial evaluation of the male should also include one or more semen analyses (SAs) ... at least two SAs, ideally obtained at least one month apart

sources.title: Time to pregnancy in subfertile women in German gynecological practices: analysis of a representative cohort of more than 60,000 patients
sources.claim: Among subfertile women, 36.8% became pregnant in the first year of observation; highest cumulative pregnancy rate 74.8% in women 18-30.
sources.quote: A total of 22,744 patients became pregnant during the first year of observation (36.8 %) ... highest cumulative pregnancy rate was seen in women between 18 and 30 years of age (74.8 %)
